headline: Williams-Sonoma: every brand grows, comparable sales up 5.1%, and EPS up 12% to $2.19 once tariff refunds are stripped out
takeaway: Comparable brand revenue rose 5.1% and adjusted EPS 11.7% to $2.19, in line with forecasts once a $29 million tariff refund is excluded; reported EPS was $2.38. But the company only reiterated its full-year outlook, which implies a slower holiday quarter, and the shares fell 15% on the day.
results: Williams-Sonoma reported net revenue growth of 5.8% for the quarter ended November 1, with comparable brand revenue up 5.1% and every brand and channel positive. GAAP operating margin was 18.9% and GAAP EPS $2.38, up 21.4%. Excluding refunds of tariffs paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, non-GAAP operating margin was 17.4%, up 0.4 points, and non-GAAP EPS $2.19, up 11.7% and roughly in line with the consensus.

Non-GAAP gross margin was 46.2%, up 0.1 points, as occupancy leverage and higher merchandise margins offset 0.5 points of extra supply-chain costs from higher oil prices. The GAAP gross margin of 47.6% included a 1.4-point benefit from the tariff refund. SG&A fell to 28.8% of revenue on a non-GAAP basis.

Inventories rose 7.3% to $1.64 billion. The company held $992 million of cash, generated $279 million of operating cash flow and returned $253 million through $163 million of buybacks and $90 million of dividends. It has collected substantially all of its $197.8 million tariff refund claim.
mgmt: Chief executive Laura Alber said every brand and channel delivered a positive comp and that the company’s design advantages and direct-sourcing model allow it to increase full-price selling while giving customers quality and value. She said its ten brands and integrated operating platform convert demand into profitable growth.

Williams-Sonoma reiterated fiscal 2026 guidance for net revenue growth of 4.7% to 7.2%, comparable growth of 4.0% to 6.5% and a non-GAAP operating margin of 17.8% to 18.2%, with interest income of about $30 million.
view: Williams-Sonoma — owner of Pottery Barn, West Elm and its namesake kitchen brand — has been one of the best-run retailers of the past decade, and this quarter continued that record. Positive comparable sales in every brand at a time when the US housing market remains frozen, and furniture demand is closely tied to home moves, is a real achievement. It reflects the company’s heavy investment in its own design and direct sourcing, which lets it sell more at full price and protect margins that are close to double those of most furniture retailers.

The tariff refunds deserve careful handling, and the company handles them well by excluding them from adjusted results. The refunds of IEEPA tariffs flatter reported profit this year but will not repeat, so the underlying EPS growth of 12% is the right number to judge. Higher oil prices are now adding freight costs, which cost half a point of margin this quarter, and inventory growing faster than sales is worth monitoring heading into the holidays.

The 15% fall shows how high expectations were. Holding the full-year range after a solid third quarter implies the holiday quarter will grow more slowly, and investors who had paid a premium for steady beats-and-raises took that as a sign that the momentum is fading. After the drop the stock trades at around 21 times earnings, still a premium for a home-furnishings retailer. That premium rests on Williams-Sonoma’s ability to keep margins near 18% through the housing cycle. If mortgage rates fall and home sales recover, its operating leverage would lift earnings sharply; until then, it is a high-quality company growing in the mid-single digits.
watch: Watch holiday-quarter comparable sales against the full-year range, gross margin as freight costs rise with oil, inventory levels, and any sign of recovery in US home sales.
